solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Setting for Gothic masterpiece which art restorer has framed

indicators.note: a frame surrounds a picture, so the run of words holds the solution inside its borders

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the whole second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A restorer has put a frame round a great Gothic work of art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Which art' sounds like a phrase from the Lord's Prayer, tempting a search for ART alone; the answer is read straight through whiCH ART RESTorer.
explanation.definitionFit: The cathedral at Chartres in northern France is among the finest examples of Gothic architecture, so the town is the setting for that masterpiece.

clue.text: Loud laugh an orphaned girl heard, folk partying

indicators.note: what is heard is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: a hoot is a loud burst of laughter
Little Orphan Annie is the famous orphaned girl of the comic strip and musical; 'an Annie' said quickly

explanation.surface: Someone hears an orphan girl's loud laugh while folk are having a party.
explanation.walkthrough: The orphaned girl is Annie, from the comic strip and musical Annie; 'an Annie' run together gives the middle and end of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A hootenanny is an informal gathering where folk musicians play and people dance, so it is folk people partying.

clue.text: Leaving steak and bread roll unfinished, dance

indicators.note: something unfinished lacks its end, so each word loses its final letter

blocks.note: rump steak, a cut from the hindquarters, without its last letter
a bap is a soft British bread roll, here without its last letter

explanation.surface: A diner walks away from half-eaten steak and roll to go dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: Steak here is RUMP and the roll is a BAP, a soft flat bread roll common in Britain; both are cut short before joining.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a ballroom and Latin American dance of Cuban origin with a distinctive hip movement.

clue.text: Herb blended with cool new French cheese

indicators.note: blending mixes ingredients together until their original order is lost

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A recipe note: mix a herb into chilled fresh French cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cool' and 'new' read as describing the cheese, but they are letters thrown in with the herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Reblochon is a soft washed-rind cow's milk cheese from the Savoie region of the French Alps.

clue.text: Doubt 1,000 lost in crush

indicators.note: what is lost is no longer there, so that letter drops out

blocks.note: to scrumple is a British word meaning to crush or crumple
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, the letter removed

explanation.surface: Fears that a thousand people died in a crowd crush.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrumple, a British variant of crumple, loses its Roman thousand from the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A scruple is a moral qualm or hesitation, so it is a doubt about whether something is right.

clue.text: Pretty bashful when indeterminate Spice Girl enters

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: coy means shy or bashful
two Spice Girls were called Mel (Mel B and Mel C), so the name alone does not say which

explanation.surface: A shy young woman blushes prettily as a pop star walks in.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spice Girls were a 1990s British pop group with two members named Mel, which is why the clue calls her indeterminate.
explanation.definitionFit: Comely is an old-fashioned adjective for attractive or good-looking, matching pretty as a description.

clue.text: Material OK to be dropped by large helicopter

indicators.note: something dropped is let go, so those letters fall away

blocks.note: the Chinook is a big twin-rotor military helicopter
taken as written, the letters removed

explanation.surface: Supplies are cleared for a drop from a heavy-lift helicopter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' looks like cargo for the airdrop, but it is the definition: cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Chino is a hard-wearing twill cotton fabric, best known from the trousers made of it.

clue.text: Microwave producer not German, surprisingly

indicators.note: a surprising result is not what was expected, so the letters come out in an unexpected order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Remarking that a microwave oven turns out not to be German-made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Microwave producer' reads like an appliance maker, but it is the component that generates the waves.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnetron is the vacuum tube in radar sets and microwave ovens that generates microwave radiation.

clue.text: Escort which motorist doesn’t use any more?

definitions.text: which motorist doesn’t use any more

blocks.note: first meaning: to guide or accompany someone

blocks.clueFragment: which motorist doesn’t use any more
blocks.note: second meaning: the metal once added to petrol and since phased out

explanation.surface: An old Ford Escort that drivers no longer use.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ford Escort was a popular British family car, steering towards cars; leaded petrol has been banned, so motorists no longer use the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to guide someone along; as a noun it is the toxic metal formerly added to petrol.

clue.text: On which you might apply to get married

blocks.note: to send for something is to send to get it
M is the standard abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: Applying for a marriage licence on the right paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as one sentence about wedding paperwork; the last four words split off as the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Applications are written on official printed documents with blanks to fill in, so it is what you apply on.

clue.text: Counter Charles built almost totally cracked

indicators.note: almost means nearly but not quite, so the word stops one letter short

blocks.note: a bar is a counter where drinks are served
Charles III is the British king
built is made, without its final letter

explanation.surface: Something King Charles built nearly fell apart with cracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counter' looks like a verb opposing Charles, but it is a noun, the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Barking mad is British slang for completely insane, and cracked is an informal word for crazy.

clue.text: Reform encountered a report of increased opposition

indicators.note: a report is something spoken and heard, so the sound counts and not the spelling

blocks.note: to meet someone is to encounter them
taken as written
more enemies means increased opposition

explanation.surface: A political reform drew a report of growing resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' does double service in the surface; the opposition is plural people, more foes.
explanation.definitionFit: To metamorphose is to change completely in form or nature, which is to reform or be transformed.

clue.text: Nuclear physicist that woman’s cross with battles to have sex on top

indicators.note: in a down entry what goes on top comes first in the reading

blocks.note: the rut is the mating season of deer, when stags fight each other for the chance to mate
her is the possessive for a woman
to ford a river is to cross it

explanation.surface: An angry woman and her battles over who gets to be on top in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battles to have sex' together describe the rut, when stags fight for mates; 'cross' is a verb, not anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest Rutherford, the New Zealand-born scientist, discovered the atomic nucleus and is called the father of nuclear physics.

clue.text: Being friendly, match oddly starts with hostility

indicators.note: odd positions are first, third, fifth, so only those letters are kept
what something starts with comes at its beginning, so that piece goes in front

blocks.note: war is open hostility
the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A sporting match that oddly turns friendly after a hostile start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being friendly' reads like an adjective phrase, but it names the quality, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Warmth is the quality of affection and cordiality, the state of being kind and welcoming towards others.

clue.text: Quiet complaint from Spooner, crushing rock

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words

blocks.note: quiet is still, a complaint is a moan; swap their opening sounds

explanation.surface: Spooner grumbles quietly while some rock is being crushed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crushing' looks like Spooner's action, but it describes the rock: one that crushes grain.
explanation.definitionFit: A millstone is one of the pair of heavy round stones that grind grain in a mill, a rock used for crushing.

clue.text: European rifled our Pimm’s store

indicators.note: to rifle through something is to rummage and leave it in disorder

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
taken as written

explanation.surface: A foreigner raided our stock of Pimm's.
explanation.walkthrough: Pimm's is a British gin-based summer drink; 'store' looks like the supply being raided but is the definition, a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: An emporium is a large retail shop selling many kinds of goods, so it is a store.

clue.text: Light green tailored coat is hip

indicators.note: tailoring cuts and reshapes cloth, so the letters are recut into a new form

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fashion verdict: a pale green fitted coat is trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light green' reads as the coat's colour, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pistachio is the pale yellowish-green colour of the nut's kernel, used as a name for that shade.

clue.text: Relative finishes off gin and tonic and Scotch to relax

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its end, so only the last letters are kept

blocks.note: an uncle is a family relative
the final letters of the three drinks

explanation.surface: An uncle downs a G and T and a whisky to unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finishes off' looks like drinking up, but it takes the last letters; 'and' between the drinks is just joining them.
explanation.definitionFit: To unclench a fist or jaw is to release tension from it, which is to let it relax.

clue.text: Lord Muck’s greeting brothers and sisters, hugging any number

indicators.note: to hug is to wrap your arms round, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: hi is a greeting
sibs is short for siblings
N stands for any number in algebra

explanation.surface: A self-important man greets his siblings with hugs all round.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Muck is British slang for a man who behaves as if he is grand; the 's is 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: His Nibs is a mocking title for a self-important man, the same jokey sense as Lord Muck.

clue.text: Sikh family name two thirds of military academy

indicators.note: two thirds of a nine-letter word keeps six letters, here the opening ones

blocks.note: Sandhurst is the British Army's officer training academy; its first six of nine letters

explanation.surface: A Sikh surname shares much with a British military academy.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandhurst, in Berkshire, is where British Army officers train.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandhu is a common Jat clan surname among Sikhs from the Punjab region of India and Pakistan.

clue.text: French composer’s works should exclude English, OK?

indicators.note: to exclude is to leave out, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: Erik Satie was a French composer, with the possessive s
works is a British word for a factory
E is the abbreviation for English, the letter removed

explanation.surface: Asking whether a French composer's output may omit English pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works' suggests musical compositions next to the composer, but it is a factory; the removed E comes from Satie's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Satisfactory means acceptable or good enough, which is just what OK means.

clue.text: Lift carrying tons, lifting in shop?

indicators.note: in a down entry what is carried rides on top, so that piece comes first

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for tons
to heft is to lift something heavy

explanation.surface: A shop's goods lift hauls heavy tons of stock.
explanation.walkthrough: Shoplifting is stealing; the question mark flags that lifting here means stealing, not raising.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting is slang for stealing, and stealing from a shop is a form of the crime of taking property.

clue.text: Judge weak king

blocks.note: a thin argument is a weak one
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge' looks like a noun naming a feeble ruler, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To think something is to consider or hold an opinion about it, which is to judge.

clue.text: Mother picked up minute shells, etc

indicators.note: in a down entry picking up raises the letters, so they read from the bottom

blocks.note: ma is an informal word for mother
mo is British slang for a moment, as in 'half a mo'

explanation.surface: A mother collected tiny seashells and other bits on the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' reads as tiny, describing the shells, but it is a short time.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammo is short for ammunition, which includes artillery shells along with bullets and cartridges.

clue.text: Make poor little monkey in charge of his bananas

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters go wild

blocks.note: a mischievous child is called a little monkey or an imp
to be over something is to be in charge of it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheeky monkey in charge of the bananas makes someone poorer.
explanation.walkthrough: Bananas sits naturally beside a monkey as food, but it signals craziness; 'little monkey' is a naughty child.
explanation.definitionFit: To impoverish someone is to reduce them to poverty, which is to make them poor.

clue.text: Carbon atom with extra electrons goes round star

indicators.note: going round something encircles it, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: an atom that has gained or lost electrons is a charged ion
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A chemistry picture: a charged carbon atom orbiting a star.
explanation.walkthrough: The science words all point to astrophysics, but 'star' is a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a celebrated person widely admired, so a star of film or music is an icon.

clue.text: House and home upright

blocks.note: HO is the abbreviation for house
a nest is a home, especially a cosy one

explanation.surface: A house and a home, both standing straight and true.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upright' sounds like a house standing straight, but it describes a person of good character.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright person is morally sound and truthful, which is what honest means.

clue.text: Pale fizzy drink made with Oxo?

blocks.note: Oxo is a British brand of stock cube
ade is a fizzy fruit drink, as in lemonade

explanation.surface: A queasy-sounding pale fizzy drink brewed from a stock cube.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pale' looks like a colour describing the drink but is a noun, a fence of stakes; the question mark admits a drink made with Oxo is a stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale is a pointed wooden stake in a fence, and a stockade is a defensive barrier built of such stakes.
